messages:
maria: Quick sync  we need to finalize Q2 sprint priorities for private deployment packaging. Field NetOps pulled three recurring asks: per-tenant IP preservation, an operator-shim upgrade lane, and customer-managed peering (BGP). Can we agree on owners and concrete launch gates?

jonah: +1. Let's rank by customer impact vs eng risk. IP preservation = high impact / high risk. Operator shim = medium/medium. BGP peering = high impact / low-medium risk (mostly config + docs).

kevin: From eng: IP preservation will touch installer, tenant operator, and possibly CNI hooks. Options: hostNetwork flag, explicit static SNAT mapping, or an IP reservation table. We need a migration tool for remaps. Risk vectors: kube-proxy restart, CNI reapply, and node replacement flows.

kevin: Minimal canary config to start with:```canary: percent: 3 max_downtime: 5m rollback: cpu_error_threshold: 2%```

sara: Ops asks: e2e upgrade harness that does: deploy tenant, snapshot pre-upgrade egress IPs, run upgrade, validate IPs unchanged when opted-in, and simulate failures + rollback. Also need a per-tenant opt-in runbook for NetOps.

ashley: Product tradeoffs: mark IP preservation as opt-in for GA to reduce scope. But UX must make opt-in explicit (installer flag + operator annotation). If customers assume default reservation, we risk support escalations and billing confusion. Need SOW language for reserved IP capacity.

maria: Draft launch gates: docs & runbook published (installer + operator), e2e upgrade tests pass (2 consecutive runs incl disruption), canary rollout automation in CI, 2 field beta customers committed, support playbook + escalation path, KMS/audit checks for operator changes.

maria: Proposed phases: Phase 0 (internal spike): operator shim prototype + installer hooks, build e2e harness. Phase 1 (beta): opt-in IP-preserve with 2 customers, run 3% canary for 24h, collect metrics. Phase 2 (GA): broader opt-in exposure (UI/installer), optional SLA add-on.

jonah: For BGP peering, ship as config-only first. Provide sample Terraform + BGP policy doc. Low engineering risk, high field value.

kevin: I'll own the operator shim spike. Plan: 2-week spike to validate hostNetwork toggle + failover scenarios. After spike I will open RFC with compatibility matrix and test artifacts.

sara: I'll own e2e harness and runbooks. Kevin, please send a concise list of failure modes we should cover so I can translate into tests. Need a nightly CI job to run upgrade verification for duration of beta.

ashley: I'll draft customer comms and opt-in billing language, and coordinate beta invites with CS.

deploy-bot: CI: privdeploy/upgrade-spike job scheduled for next sprint (https://ci.internal/jobs/privdeploy-upgrade-spike) :robot_face:

maria: Owners recap: kevin (operator spike), sara (e2e & runbooks), ashley (comms & SOW), jonah (prioritization & peering docs).

maria: Action items before Wed 11am check-in: kevin open RFC, sara scope e2e tests, ashley draft comms, jonah produce sample Terraform snippet for peering. Ping if blockers. :calendar:

kevin: One more item: define rollback window and metrics. I'll propose thresholds in the RFC.

jonah: Suggested rollback triggers: sustained connection_errors > 0.5% for 5m OR ip-delta > 0.1% after canary. Also monitor DNS timeouts and TCP RST spikes.

maria: Good. I'll update the roadmap doc with these gates and timelines. If anyone hits blockers, post here or DM. :thumbsup:
